name: Marketplace sellers (Daraz, Noon, Amazon)
sector: 7.M Digital economy, social and public sector

problems.words: Payout is less than I expected and I can't see why
quick_ideas: Line up one month's settlement report against your orders, so each deduction becomes visible
Group the deductions by type once, so repeat charges stand out.

workzap_build.text: a payout reconciler that reads every settlement and matches each fee, commission, penalty and refund to its order.

problems.ask_first: Which marketplace's payouts confuse you most?
problems.free_stops: How the reconciler reads each marketplace's reports is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one recent payout against that period's orders and note each deduction reason, so you can see what is shrinking collections.
Give one person a fixed weekly payout check in one notebook, so missing deductions are spotted before they pile up.

problems.words: Fees keep changing; I don't know my real margin per item
quick_ideas: Work out what is left from one sale of your top items after commission, shipping, storage and returns
Flag the items that come out thin or negative for a price or listing review.

workzap_build.text: a true-margin view per SKU that updates as fees, shipping, storage and returns change.

problems.ask_first: Which item group do you worry about most, the fast sellers or the ones with high fees?
problems.free_stops: The cost model per marketplace goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Pick a few best selling items and note what remains after marketplace charges and delivery, so weak items stop hiding inside total sales.
Give one person a single margin notebook for key items, so price and reorder decisions rely on one current view.

problems.words: Penalised for late dispatch because orders came in overnight
quick_ideas: Pack overnight orders first thing each morning before anything else
Note each late-dispatch warning with its cause, so the pattern becomes clear.

workzap_build.text: a dispatch board showing orders at risk of missing handover time, with WhatsApp alerts to packers.

problems.ask_first: How many orders usually arrive overnight, and is it every night or only during sales?
problems.free_stops: The alert timings and board set-up are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count overnight orders and compare them with what gets packed before midday, so the real morning dispatch backlog becomes visible.
Give one person the morning handover for overnight orders in one written list, so dispatch starts before other shop work pulls staff away.

problems.words: Stock sent to the marketplace warehouse doesn't match what they received
quick_ideas: Photograph and list every carton before an inbound shipment leaves
Compare sent against received as soon as the receipt appears, while a claim is still possible.

workzap_build.text: an inbound tracker comparing sent and received quantities for every shipment, with claim reminders before deadlines pass.

problems.ask_first: Is the shortage usually a few pieces in many cartons, or whole cartons going missing?
problems.free_stops: The tracking and claim workflow is covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count units per carton before each warehouse transfer and compare them with received units, so shortages are tied to a specific shipment.
Give one person the transfer log and carton check before stock leaves, so every warehouse sendout has one clear record.

problems.words: Storage fees eating me on slow items
quick_ideas: List the items with no recent sales and decide for each to bundle, discount or stop reordering
Send smaller inbounds of slow movers, so less sits in paid storage.

workzap_build.text: a reorder view using sales speed and lead time per SKU, flagging slow movers before storage fees build.

problems.ask_first: Is it a handful of items that sit for months, or a large part of what you hold?
problems.free_stops: The reorder rules per SKU are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the slow stock area and note which marketplace items have sat untouched all week, so storage-heavy lines are easy to spot.
Give one person a fixed weekly slow-stock review in one notebook, so reorder decisions stop adding to paid storage.

problems.words: Sold out on campaign day and lost ranking
quick_ideas: Put the inbound cut-off for the next big sale in your calendar now
Plan stock for top items from last campaign's sales rather than guesswork.

workzap_build.text: a campaign-day checklist covering stock, approved prices and staff rota, sent to the team with reminders before each event.

problems.ask_first: Did you run out of your top items, or of items you did not expect to sell?
problems.free_stops: The checklist and timing for each campaign go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare campaign day sell-through on top items with what was on hand that morning, so short planning shows up item by item.
Give one person the job of writing next campaign stock needs in one list, so replenishment stops being a last-minute guess.

problems.words: Same stock on Daraz and our website and we oversell
quick_ideas: Keep one master stock count and update every channel from it
Hold back a small buffer on each channel for fast sellers, so one sale doesn't oversell another.

workzap_build.text: multi-channel stock sync with buffer rules, so Daraz, Noon, Amazon and your own site draw from one count.

problems.ask_first: How often does an oversell happen, every week or only on busy days?
problems.free_stops: The sync design and buffer rules are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count oversold items from this week and note where stock differed between channels, so the worst overlap points are clear.
Give one person one shared stock list to update at set times daily, so channel quantities stay closer to reality.

problems.words: Buyer questions in seller centre go unanswered for days
quick_ideas: Give one person fixed daily time for seller-centre messages
Turn the most repeated questions into clearer listing text, so fewer get asked.

workzap_build.text: a shared reply library and a daily list of unanswered buyer messages by marketplace, with ageing.

problems.ask_first: Are the unanswered questions about stock and delivery, or about the product itself?
problems.free_stops: The reply library and routing are prepared in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count unanswered buyer messages at the same time each day this week, so the backlog size is clear to everyone.
Give one person a fixed daily message slot and one place to note pending replies, so buyer questions stop sitting for days.

problems.words: Every morning I download reports from three portals into Excel
quick_ideas: Decide the few numbers you truly need each day and stop building the rest
Keep all exports in one dated folder, so nothing is hunted for.

workzap_build.text: one combined daily sales view across marketplaces and countries, without downloads.

problems.ask_first: Which of the three reports do you use most each morning?
problems.free_stops: Which reports are pulled and how they combine is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which figures you actually read from each morning report this week, so wasted downloading work is easier to cut.
Give one person one written morning checklist for the required reports, so the routine stays consistent when someone is absent.

problems.words: Staff member handling the account left and nobody knows the process
quick_ideas: Write down the main weekly seller-account tasks while someone still remembers them
Make sure the business, not one person, holds the account access.

workzap_build.text: a task checklist for seller-centre work with reminders, so any staff member could pick it up.

problems.ask_first: Which job is most at risk now, listing updates, order handling or claims and returns?
problems.free_stops: The task list and handover set-up are built out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Watch this week's account work and note every repeated task in one notebook, so handover gaps stop surprising you.
Give one staff member the job of updating a single process notebook after account work, so leavers take less knowhow with them.

never_say: Anything about how a suspension appeal, IP complaint or policy dispute will turn out.
Typical marketplace fee levels, return rates or ranking promises.
Advice on VAT, GST, customs or product certification — say "talk to your accountant or customs agent".
Help with review manipulation, duplicate accounts, fake orders or others' trademarks in listings.
Any request for seller-centre passwords, OTPs, API keys or bank details.

sample_reply.person: Can you suggest a fix for our Noon payouts? They never match what we think we sold.
sample_reply.pi:
Sure, you can start on this now, and the first steps are simple.
First, line up one month's settlement report against your orders, so every deduction becomes visible.
Second, group those deductions by type once, so repeated charges stand out across Noon and Amazon.
On top of this, Workzap could arrange: a reconciler that reads each settlement, matches every line to an order and lists anything that doesn't add up.

Would you like me to prepare a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
